title: ASI Extracted Item
description: Schema for one current-snapshot ASI extracted item produced from one canonical source document.

itemId.description: Stable ID for this extracted item. Suggested form: extract:<DOC_ID>:<kind>:<normalizedKey>:<occurrenceNumber>. occurrenceNumber is a three-digit local sequence number for multiple extracted items with the same DOC_ID, kind, and normalizedKey.

key.description: Human-facing key, literal term, boundary phrase, or relation name.

normalizedKey.description: Deterministic normalized form used for matching and sorting.

context.description: Optional local context explaining where this item applies.

searchText.description: Search-oriented text. It may repeat terms and aliases intentionally.

flags.description: Structured attention flags. Empty array means no special handling is currently requested.

extractedItemKind.description: Semantic category of the extracted item. Source locations must use CMR-native sourceHints rather than invented section anchors.

oneOf.description: Document-level domain, ownership area, or non-ownership area. Use for what a document owns, primarily covers, or explicitly does not own.
Literal term, field name, phrase, named concept, or vocabulary item that may need routing. Same literal term across documents does not automatically mean same semantic meaning.
Distinction or X-is-not-Y rule, such as stateUpdate is not committed state mutation or acknowledgement is not Job success.
Meaningful relation between documents, terms, concepts, or authority areas, including support, dependency, load-with, neighboring authority, or non-equivalence.
Search or retrieval synonym. Alias does not mean source-defined term unless the canonical source explicitly defines or uses it.
Observation that the source document may be ambiguous, under-named, weakly worded, missing a useful boundary, or worth improving. This is not source patch approval.
Hint that the item affects implementation, schemas, code, command surfaces, adapters, or runtime behavior. This does not become implementation authority by itself.
Fallback for useful extracted material that does not fit current categories. Use sparingly; frequent use means the schema likely needs another kind.

sectionHint.description: CMR-native section, rule, paragraph, or range reference when available. Do not use this as an invented ASI anchor.

loadBasis.description: Reason category explaining why this document appears in a routing hint. It does not make the document authoritative by itself.

oneOf.description: Document is the primary source owner for the concept.
Card or item directly matches this document's indexed domain or vocabulary.
Document owns the boundary needed to avoid a wrong answer.
Document is useful supporting context but not the primary route.
Document is commonly loaded together with the primary route.
Document is a weak or possible route. Use candidateLoad rather than loadFirst for this basis.
Route is inferred from another source reference and needs caution.
Route exists because an audit decision accepted or required it.
Route exists because a supervisor decision accepted or required it.
Strongly supported by source or accepted workflow evidence.
Reasonably supported but may need later review or cross-document confirmation.
Weak or tentative support; use cautiously.
Requires audit, supervisor review, or stronger source evidence before relying on it.
Requires supervisor/user judgment before affected downstream use. May be emitted by any ASI workflow. Handled by Supervisor.
Meaning likely depends on comparison with other documents. Emitted by Extractor, BatchAuditor, TerminologyInferrer, or Indexer. Handled by BatchAuditor or CrossBatchAuditor.
Canonical source may need clearer wording, a missing boundary, compact term, or better source heading. Handled by Supervisor first; SourcePatcher only acts after explicit approval.
May need a better name, ASI alias, boundary phrase, relation name, or source-term proposal. Handled by TerminologyInferrer.
Plausible but weakly grounded in source. Handled by BatchAuditor, CrossBatchAuditor, Indexer, or Supervisor if final routing would depend on it.
Same literal key appears in more than one context and may not mean the same thing. Default handling is split, not merge, unless audit/supervisor decision says otherwise.
Affected output cannot proceed because a required audit, cross-batch, or supervisor decision is unresolved. Handled by Supervisor or the workflow owning the missing decision.
